newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares close up as budget countdown begins.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares close up as budget countdown begins.

text.p: Bombay shares closed higher on Monday as speculators bought on hopes of a market-friendly federal budget, traders said.
India's 1997/98 budget is due on February 28.
"Everyone's placing their bets on a good budget now," said a trader at a foreign brokerage.
Bombay's benchmark stocks index closed 38.12 points, or 1.12 percent higher, at a provisional 3445.34.
Traders said volumes were speculator-driven though there were stray fund bids in pivotals MTNL, Siemens and oil firm HPCL.
Some funds were buyers in shares of cement maker ACC, which has fallen sharply on the back of weak cement prices and an industrial slowdown.
"They're probably looking at the stock as a long-term investment after its recent fall," the trader said.
But traders said most foreign investors were on the sidelines as the macro-economic picture remained cloudy.

The Reserve Bank of India's latest report depicted government finances under strain and raised worries about an industrial slowdown, high real and nominal interest rates and a decline in the growth of exports.
Industrial production grew by 9.8 percent in April-October 1996, down from 11.7 percent in the same period a year ago.
Former finance minister Manmohan Singh also expressed worries about the economy in a newspaper interview.
He said the United Front government had fallen short of its economic targets, and had failed to win investors' confidence.

"That is the political reality. And the political reality is that we have a hotch-potch coalition which has not even been able to implement what it agreed in its common minimum programme," Singh was quoted as saying in the Economic Times.
Singh said the government had "broadly continued" the reforms initiated by the Congress Party, but "in a manner which does not generate enough confidence".
Banks and government offices closed for Moslem festival.
